title: Pilgrimage: Sarnath
hook: the Deer Park where the first sermon was given

segments.voice: Yesterday's pilgrimage went to Bodh Gaya: a tower, a tree, and many schools in one shade. Your line was where he woke. Where was your one good place to sit? Day one thousand three hundred ninety-four.

Five men are sitting in a park near the city of Benares when they see someone walking toward them on the road. They know him. He used to fast and strain alongside them, and then he quit, and started eating again. They had decided he'd gone soft. So they make a pact: when he gets here, nobody stands up. Nobody takes his bowl. Maybe offer him a seat, if he insists. Then he comes closer, and something about the way he walks undoes the whole plan. One gets up and takes his robe. Another sets out water. Someone offers a seat. The park was full of deer. The talk he gave there is the reason pilgrims still come. Today, the third stop: Sarnath.
screen: `FIVE OLD FRIENDS MAKE A PACT.` → `NOBODY STANDS UP.` → `EVERYBODY STANDS UP.`

segments.voice: First, the place. The texts call it Isipatana, the deer park near Benares. Today it is Sarnath, a quiet green with the ruins of old monasteries and a great round stupa of brick and stone. Pilgrims walk around it, and some sit on the grass and listen to the teaching read aloud. Second, the talk. The discourse is called Setting in Motion the Wheel of the Teaching. It begins not with doctrine but with a warning about two dead ends: chasing pleasure, and punishing the body. The Buddha had tried both. Between them, he says, is a middle way, and it leads to peace and to awakening. Third, the four truths. There is suffering. It has a cause, the craving that keeps reaching for more. It can end. And there is a path to its ending. Here is the detail worth keeping. In the discourse, each truth comes with a job. Suffering is to be understood. Craving is to be let go. The ending is to be realized. The path is to be walked. These are not four statements to agree with. They are four tasks. Fourth, the moment it lands. As the Buddha speaks, one of the five, Kondanna, sees it for himself: whatever arises also passes away. The Buddha says, Kondanna has understood. And the text says the gods shout the news from one heaven to the next: at Benares, in the deer park, the wheel has been set rolling.
screen: `ISIPATANA, THE DEER PARK.` · `NEITHER PLEASURE NOR PUNISHMENT.` · `FOUR TRUTHS, FOUR TASKS.` · then, large: `THE WHEEL SET ROLLING.`

segments.voice: Here is a way to sit in the deer park, if you'd like. Settle, and breathe out slowly. Then say the four truths quietly, one per breath, the way they were first spoken. There is suffering. There is a cause of suffering. There is an end of suffering. There is a path. Say them again, and this time add each task under your breath: understand, let go, realize, walk. Then let the words go and just breathe on the grass with the deer. The bell holds the time.
Pilgrimage. The road to the holy places. Its third stop is Sarnath, the deer park where the Buddha set the wheel of the teaching rolling. Today's word.
Your line: where he taught. Today, when something goes wrong, try one of the four tasks on it: understand it before you fix it. Day one thousand three hundred ninety-four.

howItsDone: Pilgrims visit Sarnath near Varanasi to walk around the great stupa, see the ruins of ancient monasteries, and chant or listen to the discourse on setting the wheel of the teaching in motion.

myth: the Buddha's first listeners at the deer park welcomed him gladly from the start
the five had agreed not to stand up for him. when he came near, they stood anyway.
in the discourse, each of the four truths comes with a task
suffering understood, craving let go, the ending realized, the path walked.
the talk begins with the middle way between two extremes
it warns against chasing pleasure and punishing the body before it gives the four truths.

fork.setup: you're one of the five. your old companion, who gave up the hard fasting, is walking toward you. you agreed not to stand. what do you do?
options: keep your pact and stay seated.
get up, take his robe and set out water.
fork.reveal: the pact fell apart. as he came near, they got up, took his bowl and robe, and set out a seat and water.

original.note: Pali dhammacakka: the wheel of the teaching, set rolling at the deer park.

trapdoor: what you thought: Sarnath is where the Buddha gave a sermon.
what it means: the deer park where he met old companions and taught the middle way and four truths, each with a task.
what a scholar hears: Isipatana, the Dhammacakkappavattana discourse, and Kondanna's insight that whatever arises passes away.

notes: Hook paraphrases Mahavagga 1.6: the group of five agree not to rise, take his bowl and robe, but to offer a seat if he wishes; as he approaches they cannot keep it. Confirm details.

SN 56.11 paraphrased: the two extremes, the middle way, the four truths and their three phases including the tasks (to be fully understood, abandoned, realized, developed). Confirm the simplified task wording.
Kondanna's insight 'whatever is subject to arising is subject to cessation' and the devas' proclamation at Isipatana near Baranasi are paraphrased. Confirm.
Sarnath described as a green with monastery ruins and the great stupa (Dhamek); 'many sit on the grass and listen' is descriptive. Confirm.
Pali dhammacakka in Devanagari: धम्मचक्क. Confirm spelling and pronunciation.
Editor: light pass; varied the word line so the pilgrimage days do not repeat one phrasing. Facts checked against Mahavagga 1.6 and SN 56.11 as paraphrased.
